$comment: Classification dimensions (REQUIREMENTS #561, #562): each dimension is ONLY its closed list of values. Which value an asset or a finding gets comes from the classification rows (classification.locked.json -- ONE generic mechanism, engine/data-model/SI-Classification.ps1); the SI fields a dimension's values are written to, and the fallback when no row matches, are the classification template's targets. A new dimension is a new item here plus its rows and target there, never code. Customer changes: Pro = one cfg.ItemOverride per dimension ('dimensions:<id>', e.g. dimensions:component -- override, disable or add); Community = dimensions.custom.json, per id. An optional 'default' (one of the values) is the fallback of every finding / single-value target on the dimension, so a customer who renames or removes the fallback value names the new one in the same item (servicenow_subci: OS / SQL / Other, default Other; os_family: default Unknown -- REQUIREMENTS #772).

dimensions.name: OS family
dimensions.description: The operating system family of an asset (and of the findings on it): Windows vs. Linux and the rest. Unknown when no source says which OS it runs, Other when the OS is known but none of the families.

dimensions.name: Patch cycle
dimensions.description: Whether a finding is fixed in the monthly patch cycle or is catch-up: its fix was released (or, without one dated update, it was first detected) within SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays (default 30) of the collection, or longer ago. No fix available when the source says none exists, or when the finding names no recommended update and nothing dates it (no single update); Unknown only for an update whose month cannot be read.

dimensions.name: ServiceNow sub-CI
dimensions.description: The ServiceNow sub-CI a finding is linked under (OS findings, SQL findings, Other findings per CI). The buckets are the customer's; default is the fallback bucket a finding no row places gets.
